q.e: Two copies make a parallelogram of area 60; the triangle is half.

q.t: Area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 4 cm (in cm²)?
q.e: Slide the triangle off one end to the other: a 9 × 4 rectangle.

q.t: Is π exactly equal to 22/7?
o: No — π is irrational; 22/7 is an approximation
q.e: π can't be written as a fraction at all (Lambert, 1761).

q.t: How long is a semicircular arc of radius r?
q.e: Half of the full circumference 2πr.

q.t: A median of a triangle divides it into two triangles that:
q.e: Equal bases (the midpoint halves the side) and the same height give equal ½ × base × height.

q.t: Using Heron's formula, find the area of a triangle with sides 3, 4, 5 (in square units).
Find the length of an arc of radius 6.3 m subtending 120° (π ≈ 22/7), in m.
q.e: Full circle 2 × 22/7 × 6.3 = 39.6; 120° is a third: 13.2.

q.t: Find the area of a sector of radius 7 cm and angle 60° (π ≈ 22/7), in cm².
A circle has circumference 44 cm. Find the area of a quadrant (π ≈ 22/7), in cm².
q.e: r = 7, full area 154, a quarter of it is 38.5.

q.t: A tyre has diameter 56 cm. How far does the car move in one turn (in cm, π ≈ 22/7)?
q.e: One turn rolls out one circumference: πd = 22/7 × 56.

q.t: A triangle has sides 7, 24, 25 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: It's right-angled (49 + 576 = 625): ½ × 7 × 24 = 84. Heron agrees.

q.t: An isosceles triangle has base 10 cm and area 60 cm². Find each equal side (in cm).
q.e: Height = 2 × 60 ÷ 10 = 12; equal side = √(5² + 12²).

q.t: A right triangle has area 54 cm² and one leg 12 cm. Find its perimeter (in cm).

q.t: Among rectangles with perimeter 40, which has the largest area?
o: They all have the same area
q.e: a + b = 20 and a(20 − a) is biggest when a = b = 10 (area 100).

q.t: On a running track, each lane is 1.22 m wider. One full circle of bend in the next lane out is longer by about:
q.e: 2π(R + 1.22) − 2πR = 2π × 1.22 ≈ 7.67 m — the radius cancels.

o: Not in general — only if extra information, like being cyclic, is known

q.t: Each wiper blade is 28 cm and sweeps 120°. Total area cleaned by two (π ≈ 22/7), in cm²:
q.e: One sector = 22/7 × 784 × 1/3 = 2464/3; two wipers double it.

q.t: Doubling every side of a triangle multiplies its area by:
q.e: Base and height both double, so ½ × base × height is multiplied by 2 × 2.

q.t: A point P is inside square ABCD. What fraction of the square is ΔPAB + ΔPCD?
q.e: Bases AB = CD = a and the two heights add up to a: ½ × a × a.

q.t: ab equals which expression (Baudhāyana's squaring of a rectangle)?
q.e: Expanding: (a² + 2ab + b² − a² + 2ab − b²)/4 = ab.

q.t: Triangle sides 10, 15, 20 cm. Its area to one decimal place (in cm²):
Radius 15 cm, chord subtending 60°. Minor segment area (π ≈ 3.14, √3 ≈ 1.73), to 2 dp:
q.e: Sector 3.14 × 225 / 6 = 117.75; equilateral triangle 1.73/4 × 225 ≈ 97.31; difference ≈ 20.44.

q.t: Two circles of radius r pass through each other's centres. The outline of the combined shape is:
q.e: Triangle with sides AB, AC, BC (all r) is equilateral, so each hidden arc is 120°; each visible arc is 240° = 2/3 of 2πr.

q.t: A semicircle on PQ versus three semicircles whose diameters together make up PQ. Which path is longer?
q.e: Semicircle length is π × radius, proportional to the diameter, and the small diameters add up to PQ.

q.t: A square inscribed in a circle of radius r covers what fraction of the circle?
q.e: Its diagonal is 2r, so its area is (2r)²/2 = 2r². 2r² ÷ πr² = 2/π ≈ 0.637.

q.t: A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle covers what fraction of it, to 3 decimal places?
q.e: Six equilateral triangles of side r: (3√3/2)r² ÷ πr² = 3√3/(2π) ≈ 0.827.

q.t: BC = l is a chord of the big circle touching the smaller concentric circle. The area between the circles is:
q.e: The radius to the touching point is ⊥ to BC and bisects it: R² − r² = (l/2)², so π(R² − r²) = πl²/4.

q.t: Semicircles are drawn on the sides of a right triangle (areas A, B on the legs, C on the hypotenuse). Then:
q.e: A semicircle on side x has area (π/8)x², and leg² + leg² = hypotenuse².

q.t: In a square of side 2, four semicircles on the sides make a 4-petal flower. Its area is:
q.e: Each petal is two segments of a radius-1 quarter circle: 2(π/4 − 1/2) = π/2 − 1. Four petals give 2π − 4.

q.t: A car wheel of radius 28 cm travels 1 km. How many COMPLETE turns does it make (π ≈ 22/7)?
q.e: One turn = 176 cm; 100000 ÷ 176 ≈ 568.2, so about 568 complete turns.
